# BH-700 Baghouse Control Narrative (Draft A)

This draft comes from the shift supervisor's email only. Every value marked **proposed** needs Operations confirmation before the integrator programs it. The open items (section 10) include decisions the email left unclear.

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

BH-700 removes dust from the kiln exhaust gas. The module controls these devices:

- ID fan F-703
- Screw conveyor SC-701
- Rotary airlock RV-702
- Inlet damper D-704
- Bleed-air damper D-706
- The pulse-cleaning rows

**Interfaces:**
- The upstream interface is the kiln feed. A kiln feed inhibit request leaves this module (OI-03).
- The downstream interface is the stack. No stack requirements appear in the email.

## 2. Equipment and tags

Refer to the instrument index for all tags. The email names these tags:

| Tag | Function |
|---|---|
| F-703 | ID fan |
| SC-701 | Screw conveyor |
| RV-702 | Rotary airlock |
| D-704 | Inlet damper |
| D-706 | Bleed-air damper |
| TT-705 | Inlet temperature |

**Tags missing from the email (OI-01):** the baghouse DP transmitter, the pulse valves per row, the kiln feed device, the airlock run-status feedback, and the damper position switches.

## 3. States and transitions (ISA-106)

| State | Entry permissive | Initiator | Automation level | Allowed exits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| STOPPED | None | Stop complete or trip complete | Automatic | STARTING |
| STARTING | Start permissives met (see the cause-and-effect chart) | Operator | Automatic after the start command | RUNNING, TRIPPED, STOPPING |
| RUNNING | Start sequence complete | Automatic | Automatic | STOPPING, TRIPPED |
| STOPPING (clean-down) | None | Operator | Automatic | STOPPED, TRIPPED |
| TRIPPED | None | Automatic | Automatic | STOPPED, after operator reset |

**Requirements:**

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BH700-001 | The module shall have only the five states in the table above. | FAT: state table walk-through |
| FR-BH700-002 | The module shall allow only the exits listed in the table. | FAT: attempt each disallowed transition |
| FR-BH700-003 | The module shall leave TRIPPED only after an operator reset. The reset shall be accepted only when the trip cause is clear. | FAT: reset with the cause active, then clear |

## 4. Regulatory control

BH-700 has no PID loops in the email. D-706 uses on/off control (FR-BH700-030). Pulse control is timer-based with two rates (FR-BH700-020 to -023).

## 5. Sequences

### 5.1 Start sequence (STARTING)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Start SC-701 and RV-702. | Both are confirmed running. | TM-01 | Go to TRIPPED. Raise the alarm. |
| 2 | Start F-703. | F-703 is confirmed running. | TM-02 | Stop the started equipment. Go to TRIPPED. |
| 3 | Wait for the fan stabilization time. | TM-03 has elapsed. | TM-03 | Not applicable |
| 4 | Open D-704. | D-704 is confirmed open. | TM-04 | Close D-704. Go to STOPPING. Raise the alarm. |
| 5 | Start pulse cleaning. | Pulse cleaning is active. | TM-05 | Raise the alarm. Continue. |

Step 1 comes before step 2 in this draft. Mike's fan-first order is OI-02.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BH700-010 | The sequence shall run the steps in the order shown. | FAT: run the sequence and check the order |
| FR-BH700-011 | The sequence shall not open D-704 until TM-03 has elapsed after F-703 is confirmed running. | FAT: check D-704 command time |
| FR-BH700-012 | Each step shall apply its timeout and failure response from the table. | FAT: force a failure at each step |

### 5.2 Stop sequence (STOPPING, clean-down)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Keep F-703, SC-701, and RV-702 running. Keep pulsing. | TM-06 has elapsed. | TM-06 | Not applicable |
| 2 | Close D-704. | D-704 is confirmed closed. | TM-04 | Raise the alarm. Continue. |
| 3 | Stop F-703. | F-703 is confirmed stopped. | TM-02 | Raise the alarm. Continue. |
| 4 | Stop pulsing. Stop RV-702, then SC-701. | Both are confirmed stopped. | TM-01 | Raise the alarm. |

The email does not give the order of the last stops or when D-704 closes during clean-down (OI-04).

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BH700-015 | The module shall pulse with F-703 running for the clean-down time in STOPPING. | FAT: stop and time the clean-down |
| FR-BH700-016 | The module shall keep SC-701 and RV-702 running during clean-down. | FAT: check status during clean-down |

## 6. Interlocks and permissives

See the BH-700 cause-and-effect chart. The chart shall hold these causes:

- The airlock stop trip (FR-BH700-040)
- The high inlet temperature action (FR-BH700-030)
- The start permissives

This section does not restate the logic.

## 7. Alarms

See the rationalized alarm database. The chart and database shall hold alarms for these conditions: high DP, high-high DP, high inlet temperature, airlock stopped, sequence step timeout, and bad PV.

## 8. Abnormal handling

### 8.1 Pulse cleaning

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BH700-020 | In RUNNING, the module shall pulse one row at a time. | FAT: observe row order |
| FR-BH700-021 | The module shall use the normal pulse interval when DP is below the high-DP pulse setpoint (SP-02). | FAT: simulate DP |
| FR-BH700-022 | The module shall use the fast pulse interval when DP is at or above SP-02. | FAT: simulate DP |
| FR-BH700-023 | The module shall return to the normal interval when DP falls below SP-02 minus the deadband (SP-06). | FAT: simulate DP falling |
| FR-BH700-024 | The module shall prompt the operator to stop the kiln feed when DP is at or above SP-03. | FAT: simulate DP; check the prompt |

### 8.2 Airlock stop

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BH700-040 | The module shall go to TRIPPED when RV-702 stops without a command. | FAT: fail RV-702 feedback |
| FR-BH700-041 | In TRIPPED, the module shall stop the equipment in the order and with the delays in the cause-and-effect chart. | FAT: trip and check the actions |

The 2019 fire may make this a safety function. Refer to the SRS if the hazard review requires it (OI-05). Do not specify SIS logic here.

### 8.3 High inlet temperature

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-BH700-030 | The module shall open D-706 when TT-705 is above SP-04. | FAT: simulate TT-705 |
| FR-BH700-031 | The module shall close D-706 when TT-705 falls below SP-04 minus the deadband (SP-07). | FAT: simulate TT-705 falling |
| FR-BH700-032 | The module shall raise the high-temperature alarm when TT-705 is above SP-04. | FAT: check the alarm |

The email gives no action if D-706 is open and TT-705 stays high (OI-06).

### 8.4 Failure conditions

| Condition | Required response | ID | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bad PV: TT-705 | Not defined | FR-BH700-050 | OI-07 |
| Bad PV: DP | Not defined | FR-BH700-051 | OI-07 |
| Comms loss to the control system | Not defined | FR-BH700-052 | OI-07 |
| Power loss and restart | Not defined | FR-BH700-053 | OI-07 |
| Fail position: D-704 | Not defined | FR-BH700-054 | OI-08 |
| Fail position: D-706 | Not defined | FR-BH700-055 | OI-08 |

The integrator shall not program these rows until the owners close the open items. Each row will get a response and test method when its item closes.

## 9. Operator interface

| Operator action | Detail |
|---|---|
| Sees | The state, equipment status, DP, TT-705, and the active pulse interval |
| Changes | Start, stop, reset, and the setpoints in the list (with the right access level) |
| Is prompted | To stop the kiln feed at high-high DP |

Operations shall sign off on the states and prompts.

### Setpoint and timer list (single source for values)

| ID | Item | Value | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| SP-01 | Normal pulse interval per row | 10 s | Proposed |
| SP-02 | High-DP pulse setpoint | 6 to 7 in. (value not decided) | OI-09 |
| SP-03 | High-high DP (kiln feed prompt) | 8 in. | Proposed |
| SP-04 | High inlet temperature (TT-705) | 450 °F | Proposed |
| SP-05 | Fast pulse interval per row | 5 s | Proposed |
| SP-06 | DP deadband | Not given | OI-09 |
| SP-07 | Temperature deadband | Not given | OI-09 |
| TM-01 | Conveyor and airlock start/stop timeout | Not given | OI-10 |
| TM-02 | Fan start/stop timeout | Not given | OI-10 |
| TM-03 | Fan stabilization time before D-704 opens | About 1 min | OI-10 |
| TM-04 | Damper travel timeout | Not given | OI-10 |
| TM-05 | Pulse start timeout | Not given | OI-10 |
| TM-06 | Clean-down time | 10 min | Proposed |

## 10. Open items

The owners and dates below are my proposals. Confirm them before issue.

| ID | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-01 | Supply the missing tags (DP transmitter, pulse valves, kiln feed device, feedback signals). | Controls lead | 2026-11-01 |
| OI-02 | Decide the start order: discharge equipment first (Dave) or fan first (Mike). The reason for fan-first is bag blinding. The risk of discharge-first is unknown. | Shift supervisor, process engineer | 2026-11-01 |
| OI-03 | Decide whether the kiln feed stops automatically or by operator action. State what happens to the kiln when BH-700 trips. | Process engineer | 2026-11-08 |
| OI-04 | Confirm the stop order and when D-704 closes. | Shift supervisor | 2026-11-01 |
| OI-05 | Review the 2019 airlock fire. Decide if the airlock-stop trip is a safety function. If it is, move it to the SRS. | Safety lead | 2026-11-15 |
| OI-06 | Define the action if TT-705 stays high with D-706 open. This may also be a safety function. | Process engineer, safety lead | 2026-11-15 |
| OI-07 | Define bad PV, comms loss, and power loss and restart responses. | Controls lead, process engineer | 2026-11-15 |
| OI-08 | Confirm fail positions for D-704 and D-706. | Process engineer | 2026-11-08 |
| OI-09 | Fix SP-02 (the email says 6 or 7 in.) and the deadbands SP-06 and SP-07. | Shift supervisor | 2026-11-01 |
| OI-10 | Set the timers TM-01 to TM-05, and confirm TM-03. | Process engineer | 2026-11-08 |
| OI-11 | Check that "quick" shutdown (FR-BH700-041) has a defined delay and order. | Shift supervisor | 2026-11-01 |
| OI-12 | Check the engineering units for DP (in. w.c. assumed) and the instrument range. | Controls lead | 2026-11-01 |

## Notes on what I changed from the email

- I chose discharge-first because it is the stated primary order. I did not choose it as the better order.
- I made the DP over 8 in. action an operator prompt, because the email says "usually shut kiln feed". That wording describes habit, not a rule.
- I left every response the email did not state (bad PV, power loss, fail positions) as an open item. I did not invent them.

I have not yet run the STE editing pass or reviewed this draft with Operations. Both are needed once the open items close.
